# Safe code review: spam-token notification filter

**Mode:** committed range `42f8946…HEAD`, as you asked. Adjudicated with two subagents; I ran the nine category passes myself.
**Scope:** 14 files, +198 −3 · base `42f8946` → `98904e8` (2 commits) · TypeScript/NestJS · jest · 9 of 9 areas had something to review · adjudicated 1 of 5.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | **Fix before opening the PR**, or show that every Transaction Service deployment already sends `trusted` |
| **Overall** | ~72 / 100 |
| **Main drag** | Regression: making `trusted` required can silently drop whole token events |
| **Fix first** | #1: make `trusted` optional and filter only on `trusted === false` |

## Scores by area (worst first)

| Area | Score | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Regression | 60 | #1 (P1), #2 (P2) |
| Testing | 85 | #3 |
| KISS | 92 | #1 also covers `OUTGOING_TOKEN` requiring a field nothing reads |
| Performance | 95 | #4 |
| Security, Bugs, Architecture, DRY, Conventions | 100 | Nothing found. License headers are present, and `LogType` was added in alphabetical order. |

## Must fix before opening

**#1 · P1 · Regression · `src/modules/hooks/routes/entities/schemas/incoming-token.schema.ts:11`** (and `outgoing-token.schema.ts:11`)
- **What:** `trusted: z.boolean()` is now required on `INCOMING_TOKEN` and `OUTGOING_TOKEN`. Both schemas are part of the `EventSchema` union.
- **Why it matters:** if a producer leaves the field out, `EventSchema.parse` rejects the whole event:
  - AMQP (`hooks.repository.ts:42`): the error is only logged, and the message is acked anyway (`queues-api.service.ts:26-35`). It is lost for good.
  - HTTP (`hooks.controller.ts:50`): the request is rejected by `ValidationPipe`.
  - Either way the cache is not cleared, so balances, collectibles, transfers and transactions go stale. All push notifications for that event are lost too, not just the spam ones.
  - `OUTGOING_TOKEN` never reads `trusted` (`event-to-notify.entity.ts:23-31`), so requiring it there adds risk and does nothing.
- **Fix:** use `trusted: z.boolean().optional()`. The repo already does this for a new producer field in `chain-update.schema.ts:8`. Or drop the field from `OUTGOING_TOKEN`. Pair this with the check change in #2.
- **Adjudication:** CONFIRMED. The validator confirmed it and the refuter could not disprove it. Impact is I3 (stale data plus lost notifications). Likelihood is L2, because it depends on the external Transaction Service rollout, which this repo can't show.

## Worth a ticket / your call

| # | P | Area | Location | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | P2 | Regression | `src/modules/notifications/domain/push/push-notification.service.ts:92` | `!event.trusted` treats a missing field as spam. BullMQ `PUSH_NOTIFICATION_EVENT` jobs queued before the deploy go straight to `processEvent` without re-parsing (`consumers/push-notification.consumer.ts:46-49`). Those have no `trusted` and get dropped, logged as `NotificationSpamTokenDropped` rather than as errors. The same happens to any event once #1 makes the field optional. | Check `event.trusted === false`, so only an explicit flag from the Transaction Service drops a notification. |
| 3 | P3 | Testing | `src/modules/hooks/routes/hooks-cache.integration.spec.ts:93` (also 109, 801, …) | Every cache-invalidation case uses `trusted: true`. Nothing shows that an untrusted (`false`) or missing-`trusted` token event still clears the cache or reaches `enqueueEvent`. There is also no unit test for a missing `trusted` in `push-notification.service.spec.ts:183-247`. | Add a `trusted: false` case to the token cache tests, plus a missing-field case after #1 and #2. |
| 4 | P3 | Performance | `src/modules/notifications/domain/push/push-notification.service.ts:93` | One `info` log per dropped spam event. Spam airdrops can hit many Safes at once, so log volume grows with that. Not adjudicated; low confidence. | Consider `debug`, or keep it and rely on log sampling. |

## Not covered

- Whether the Transaction Service already sends `trusted` on every chain. It lives in another repo, and that answer decides how likely #1 is to bite.
- I ran no tests or lint, as you asked.
- Findings #2–#4 were not sent to the validator and refuter (the 2-subagent budget went to #1). They count at full weight.

## Worth tidying

None. Nothing here is worth tidying beyond the findings above.

## Ruled out

- **The FCM payload strip** (`push-notification.service.ts:439-443`): it correctly removes the boolean from `data`, and `IncomingTokenNotification` is typed as `Omit<…,'trusted'>` to match.
- **The integration test** "suppress INCOMING_TOKEN … not trusted" isn't vacuous. It asserts that `getSubscribersBySafe` is not called, which would fail if the event got through.
